claims.statement: `GET /accounts/holdings` paginates positions, not accounts or holdings rows: `PositionRepository.get_by_user` counts `PositionModel` rows joined to the user's `AccountModel` rows, so the response `total` is a position count and one account can contribute several items whose rows may be split across page boundaries because the service only ever regroups the fetched page.

`PositionService.get_user_holdings` buckets the repository's page by `account_id`, resolves each distinct account once through `AccountService.get_account` (not once per position), converts each position via `_calculate_holdings`, and then layers account context onto the already-converted rows with `UserHoldingRead(**holding.model_dump(), account_id=account.id, account_name=account.name)`.

`PositionService.get_account_holdings` computes `total_value` and `total_profit_loss` over every position of the account (an unlimited `get_by_account` call) while returning only one paginated page of `items`, and when `account.net_deposits` is set it recomputes `total_profit_loss` as `total_value - Money(net_deposits, account.currency)` with `total_profit_loss_percent` only when `net_deposits != 0`.

`HoldingRead` carries both native-currency values (`average_cost`, `unconverted_total_value`, `unconverted_profit_loss`, `security_currency`) and account-currency values (`total_value`, `profit_loss`, `currency`, `converted_average_cost`, `converted_latest_price`); `UserHoldingRead` adds `account_id`/`account_name` and `AccountHoldingsRead` extends `PaginatedResponse[HoldingRead]` with account identity, totals, `net_deposits` and `currency`.

Authorization differs per holdings endpoint: `GET /accounts/holdings` is scoped implicitly by the repository's join on `AccountModel.user_id`, whereas `GET /accounts/{account_id}/holdings` and `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` look the account up and call `authorization_api.check_entity_owned_by_user` before delegating to `PositionService`.

`_calculate_holdings` silently skips a position whose security cannot be resolved (it logs "Security not found for position ..." and continues), so a holdings page can return fewer rows than the position count in `total`.

`PositionService.get_holdings_by_security` fills the repository's `AccountHoldingRead` placeholder rows (`total_value=0.0`, `currency=""`) with `quantity × latest close` in the security currency, `account_total_value` from `get_total_for_account` and `account_percentage` only when the account total is positive, and returns an ambiguous `([], 0)` when the security is unknown — behaviour the source marks with a TODO.

The cross-account paging loop is a browser-side safety valve in `HoldingsService.load()`: `PAGE_SIZE = 50` matches the backend `PaginationParams` default and `MAX_PAGES = 100` caps the collection at 5 000 rows, and the loop also breaks on an empty page, because the server's `total` (a position count) can be stale relative to concurrent position writes.

The `/holdings` server load is preferences-only: it returns exactly `{ holdings_table_config, group_mode, elliott_waves }` and never fetches holdings, and it reads `holdings_table`, `holdings_group` and `elliott_waves` inside a `try/catch` that treats a preferences failure as non-fatal by keeping the initial `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig(null)`, `normalizeHoldingsGroupMode(null)` and `null` fallbacks.

SSR requests that must authenticate pass the `auth_token` cookie explicitly as a Bearer override because `ApiClient.get` only sets `Authorization: Bearer` when a token override is supplied (it always sets `credentials: 'include'`); `/holdings` has no server-side 401 mapping — its post-navigation load routes a 401 through the shared `redirectOn401` seam (`goto('/auth/login?clear_session=true')`) and renders other load or persistence failures in the same page-level `holdings-error` alert instead of a Kit error page.

`/holdings` derives its header totals by bucketing `service.rows` on `row.currency` in a `SvelteMap`: it sums `total_value`, sums non-null `profit_loss` (tracking `hasProfitLoss`), accumulates `costBasis` as `quantity × (converted_average_cost ?? average_cost ?? 0)` only when positive, and computes `returnPercent` only when `costBasis > 0` — values are never summed across currency buckets.

`groupHoldings` in `stock` mode (and its legacy `company` alias) keys strictly on `security_id`, keeps first-appearance ordering, sums `quantity`/`total_value`/`unconverted_total_value` and null-preserving P/L, computes quantity-weighted `average_cost` and `converted_average_cost`, dedupes `account_names` and counts distinct accounts — and hardcodes the group `currency` to `'CAD'`, so values already converted into different account currencies are summed under a CAD label.

The `/holdings` page owns its `HoldingsService` instance instead of reading a layout context and seeds only the group mode from the server load with `setGroupBy(data.group_mode)`; a mount-time `$effect` calls `service.load()` (which never runs during SSR, so the fetch trigger stays browser-only), making grouping and every derived view a pure client-side computation that never refetches holdings, while `getHoldingsService` remains the context/custom-fetch accessor for other callers.

`HoldingsService.load()` is the browser's only holdings collector: it pages `getUserHoldings(offset, PAGE_SIZE, token)` until `offset >= total`, returns `null` on success and the caught error on failure (so the caller can route a 401 through `redirectOn401`), stores the message in `errorMessage` while keeping the previously loaded rows, stringifies non-`Error` throws, and clears the error on the next successful load.

`holdings-table.svelte` stays presentational: it derives a normalized `HoldingsTableConfig` from the `tableConfig` prop, keeps a local copy so a column drag gives immediate feedback, and emits the final clamped config once at pointer-up via `onConfigChange`, while the `/holdings` page owns persistence and pushes write failures into a `holdings-error` alert without reverting the optimistic UI change.

`holdings_table` and `holdings_group` are persisted one top-level key at a time (`patchPreferences({ holdings_table: config })` / `patchPreferences({ holdings_group: mode })`) through an injected structural prefs service instead of the module singleton, matching the backend's top-level JSONB `||` merge so a concurrent write to a different preference key cannot be dropped (nested values of the same key remain last-write-wins).

`normalizeHoldingsTableConfig` guarantees a usable config from any stored shape: non-object/missing input yields defaults, unknown column ids are dropped from `widths` and `visible`, widths are clamped by `clampColumnWidth` (non-finite → default), surviving `visible` ids are re-ordered to canonical `HOLDINGS_TABLE_COLUMN_IDS` order with the sticky column force-included, an empty or fully invalid `visible` list falls back to all columns, and the returned object never aliases the defaults.

`HOLDINGS_TABLE_STICKY_COLUMN_ID` (`security_symbol`) can never be hidden: `toggleColumnVisibility` returns the same config object unchanged for it, the display-settings menu item is `disabled`, and the table uses the constant for its sticky cell and skeleton columns, while `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig` re-adds it to any stored `visible` list.

`normalizeHoldingsGroupMode` normalizes the persisted `holdings_group` value to `'stock'` only for `'stock'` and the legacy `'company'`, and to `'none'` for every other value (including `'STOCK'`, numbers, objects and `null`), so a stored legacy mode still renders grouped while the next save writes `'stock'`.

`AccountClient.getAccountHoldings(id, token)` sends no `offset`/`limit`, so `/accounts/[id]` receives the backend defaults (offset 0, limit 50 for `PaginationParams`) while `AccountHoldingsRead.total` and the header totals cover every position of the account — meaning accounts with more than 50 positions render truncated rows next to complete totals.

The accounts dashboard `/` reads only the account list (`GET /accounts/`, ordered by account name) in its server load and defers each row's value to a client-side `GET /accounts/{id}/totals` call that `PositionService.get_total_for_account` resolves by pricing the account's positions, converting into the account currency and returning `AccountTotals` (`cost`/`value` as `Money`); the per-item state caches the result and invalidates it when a sync finishes, and the dashboard itself renders no holdings rows.

`/accounts/[id]` renders its header from `AccountHoldingsRead` and its body through the separate presentational `frontend/src/lib/components/accounts/holdings-table.svelte`, which takes `holdings` and `totalAccountValue`, has no column configuration or grouping, shows native- and account-currency values side by side when they differ, and is mounted only when `data.holdings.items.length > 0`.

The holdings read path's test suites follow the repository's mocking contract: the frontend suites mock or inject every API client and framework module that performs network or browser work (`$lib/api/accountService`, `$lib/api/userPreferencesService`, `$app/paths`, `$app/navigation`) and pin the preferences-only load contract, the paging loop, per-currency bucketing, grouping toggles and single-key preference writes, while the backend suites mock `PositionRepository`, `AccountService`, `SecurityApi` and `MarketPricesApi` and pin user isolation, pagination and per-account stamping.
